paragraphs: GovWell sells software that city and county governments use to run permitting, licensing, planning, and code enforcement work. Residents and businesses use the same system to reach services, pay, and get answers outside office hours.

Permits, plan review, and inspections are handled together in one place for staff. Licensing runs online too, with applicants filing, paying, and renewing while staff keep records and approvals on their side. Code enforcement officers track cases, schedule inspections, and follow issues to closure. The company argues that AI can do real work in these processes, reviewing applications against local code, answering resident questions, flagging violations in plans, and routing inspections.

GovWell says it was founded by the son of a general contractor who watched his father struggle to get permits quickly. Its case for existing is that local governments cannot hire software engineers at competitive salaries. Deployment strategists and configuration tooling are meant to shorten implementations against older systems.
